subject: biology
title: Human reproductive systems
key_idea: The male system makes sperm and delivers them into the female. The female system makes egg cells and provides a place for the embryo to develop. Sperm and egg cells are gametes, each adapted for its job.

blocks.text: The male system produces sperm and passes them into the female body. Each part has a job in doing this.

rows: A bag of skin that holds the testes outside the body, where it is cooler than inside.
Tubes that carry sperm from the testes to the urethra.
Adds fluid to the sperm to make semen.
Carries semen out through the penis. It also carries urine, but never at the same time.
Passes semen into the vagina during sexual intercourse.

items: Sperm are made in the testes and travel along the sperm ducts and the urethra.
The prostate gland adds fluid to make semen, and the penis delivers it into the vagina.

blocks.text: The female system makes egg cells and provides a place for a fertilised egg to develop.

rows: Make egg cells and release one about every month (and make the hormones oestrogen and progesterone).
Tubes that carry the egg cell from an ovary to the uterus. Fertilisation takes place here.
A muscular organ where an embryo implants and the fetus develops.
A ring of muscle at the lower end of the uterus. It keeps the fetus in during pregnancy.
Receives the penis and the sperm during intercourse. It is also the birth canal.

diagram.alt: An activity naming the parts of the male and female reproductive systems: testis, scrotum, sperm duct, prostate gland, urethra, penis, ovary, oviduct, uterus, cervix and vagina. Each part can be tapped to show its function.
diagram.prompt: Tap each part of the reproductive systems to learn its job, then test yourself.

parts.name: Scrotum
parts.detail: Holds the testes outside the body, where it is cooler.

parts.name: Sperm duct
parts.detail: Carries sperm from the testis to the urethra.

parts.name: Prostate gland
parts.detail: Adds fluid to sperm to make semen.

parts.name: Urethra
parts.detail: Carries semen (or urine) out through the penis.

parts.name: Penis
parts.detail: Places semen in the vagina during intercourse.

parts.name: Ovary
parts.detail: Makes egg cells and releases them.

parts.name: Oviduct
parts.detail: Carries the egg to the uterus. Fertilisation happens here.

parts.name: Uterus
parts.detail: Where the embryo implants and the fetus develops.

parts.name: Cervix
parts.detail: A ring of muscle at the base of the uterus.

parts.name: Vagina
parts.detail: Receives sperm and is the birth canal.

items: Egg cells are made in the ovaries and travel along the oviducts.
The uterus is where the fetus develops. The cervix and vagina lead out of it.

blocks.text: Male and female gametes are very different. Each is adapted to its role in fertilisation.

rows: Head with a nucleus and an acrosome, a middle piece full of mitochondria, and a tail (flagellum)
A nucleus in a large cytoplasm that contains energy stores, with a jelly coat around the outside
Cannot move by itself. It is moved along the oviduct.
Usually one released at a time

items: The **flagellum** (tail) lets the sperm swim to the egg.
Many **mitochondria** release the energy needed for swimming.
The **acrosome** contains enzymes that digest the jelly coat of the egg cell, so the sperm can get in.
**Energy stores** in the cytoplasm feed the embryo in its first days.
The **jelly coat** changes at fertilisation so that other sperm cannot enter.
Both gametes have a haploid nucleus, with half the usual number of chromosomes.
A sperm is small, motile and made in large numbers. An egg cell is large, cannot swim and is released singly.
A sperm has a flagellum, mitochondria and enzymes in the acrosome. An egg has energy stores and a jelly coat.

checks.q: State the function of the prostate gland.
checks.a: It adds fluid to the sperm to make semen.

checks.q: State three adaptive features of a sperm cell.
checks.a: A flagellum (tail), many mitochondria and enzymes in the acrosome.

checks.q: Give two differences between sperm and egg cells.
checks.a: Any two from: sperm are much smaller than egg cells; sperm can swim but egg cells cannot; sperm are made in far greater numbers than egg cells.

worked_example.question:
Once an egg cell has been released from a follicle it can be fertilised by a sperm cell.

State three adaptive features of a sperm cell.
worked_example.tip: Any three score one mark each. Name the feature. The question asks you to state, so no explanation is needed.

worked_example.question:
The male reproductive system in humans produces sperm in a liquid called semen. A scientist investigates how age affects the mean number of sperm released in one ejaculation. The table shows some of the results.

Age in years: 37–39 | 48–72
mean number of sperm released in millions: 202 | 142

Calculate the percentage decrease in mean number of sperm between men aged 37–39 and men aged 48–72.
worked_example.tip: One mark for the change and one for dividing by the starting value and multiplying by 100.
